title: The 25th Annual Putnam County Spelling Bee by Rachel Sheinkin and Wil...
transcript: I have no idea how I went so long not knowing how good of a musical The 25th Annual Putnam County Spelling Bee is. I'd never seen it, read about it, or even knowingly heard the songs, but I am finally a certified fan. With a silly premise that unfolds with a surprising amount of heart, this musical involves six kids played by adults competing in the titular bee, along with some audience members who sign up to participate before the show begins. Your role as an audience member is to attend the spelling bee, so there’s loads of opportunity for ad-libs and audience interactions, giving the whole experience a refreshing sense of presence — you're in it with them. Obviously, there's a lot of spelling in the show, but the competition is interspersed with various scenes and songs that contextualize the life of each contestant. It's a hilarious and rewarding character exploration, especially since they're kids — they wear their emotions on their sleeve, and I was so invested in them, much more than I would have imagined. The book by Rachel Sheinkin is so funny and the score by William Finn is delightful, featuring bangers such as Magic Foot and My Unfortunate Erection. Top it off with a quality and charismatic cast, and you've got an obvious hit here. I especially loved seeing Justin Cooley, and I was fortunate enough to see Emily N Rudolph make her understudy debut as Olive — she was great. Overall, the bee is a must-see. With that, another program for my collection.
